gaps.quote: Every fixed-tape procedure of the argument comes from one and the same network
gaps.note: Contradicts the paper, which says each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network (paper.tex line 116: 'Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values'). The page itself later treats different networks and frames (a route from a source frame I to a sink frame D). Correct: every procedure comes from a network of this kind, not a single shared network.

gaps.quote: so the paper fixes every intermediate frame to the identity
gaps.note: False and not a consequence of telescoping. Telescoping shows the intermediate frames cancel from the route's operator, so they do not affect the result. The paper says they are chosen to make each edge change inexpensive (paper.tex lines 824-825, 155-156: 'the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive'; 'chosen so that every edge can be implemented by smaller calls'). Setting them all to the identity would make the single edge carry the whole operator D_sink D_source^{-1}.

gaps.quote: invertible linear operator $D_\nu$ on arrays indexed by the common address set
gaps.note: The page never says that all role streams share one address set (paper.tex line 126-127: 'All role streams have the same local address set'), so the reader cannot tell what 'the common address set' is or why one operator D_nu can act on every wire's array and be compared across roles.

gaps.quote: The intermediate frames cancel and the route applies only its endpoint operator
gaps.note: The displayed product contains only edge operators, but a route passes through gates between its edges, and a gate combines several wires. The reader is not told that the whole network then acts as D_out S D_in^{-1} (paper.tex eq. common-frame-identity, lines 800-816) or why the gate sits harmlessly between consecutive edge operators; the page also never states that all incidences of one gate use the same frame, which the commuting identity needs.

gaps.term: every role keeps the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: The page has shown that role w ends with eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, which depends on w. It never says that the endpoint frames are chosen so that this operator is one and the same on every role (the shear or the simultaneous layer in the paper), and the cited claim is exactly the step the argument rests on without its content or role being stated. Also the sentence before it only shows the scratch case, which the paper takes from the construction (paper.tex lines 1273-1277).
